sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Testimonies began this week in one of the most aggressive cases the government has ever brought against a big tech company.
sentences.zh: 本周，政府针对一家大型科技公司发起的、史上最激进的诉讼之一正式开始作证。

sentences.en: And over the next eight weeks, the Federal Trade Commission will argue that Meta, the company founded by Mark Zuckerberg in his college dorm room, should be broken up.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的八周里，联邦贸易委员会将主张拆分Meta——这家由马克·扎克伯格在大学宿舍里创立的公司。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Cecilia Kang on the strange and contentious relationship between Zuckerberg and President Trump that has led to this moment
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事塞西莉亚·康将讲述扎克伯格与特朗普总统之间导致这一时刻的奇怪且充满争议的关系，

sentences.en: and what the case means for both of them.
sentences.zh: 以及这起案件对他们双方意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, April 17.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月17日，星期四。

sentences.en: Cecilia, you are talking to me from your car, I believe.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉亚，我想你现在是在车里跟我通话吧。

sentences.en: Why are you talking to me from your car?
sentences.zh: 你为什么在车里跟我通话？

sentences.en: Yeah, I had to run to my car because I'm on a lunch break during an antitrust trial where the Federal Trade Commission is seeking to break up Meta.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不得不跑回车里，因为我正在反垄断审判的午休时间，联邦贸易委员会正寻求拆分Meta。

sentences.en: And this is a really high stakes case for Meta and for Mark Zuckerberg because this case really threatens the company's entire existence.
sentences.zh: 这对Meta和马克·扎克伯格来说是一场赌注极高的官司，因为它确实威胁到了公司的整个生存。

sentences.en: It's existential because the government is trying to break up this company that he co-founded two decades ago.
sentences.zh: 这是关乎存亡的，因为政府正试图拆分这家他二十年前共同创立的公司。

sentences.en: And I have just spent the first half of this week watching Zuckerberg testify as the first and star witness in the government's case against Meta.
sentences.zh: 我刚花了本周前半段的时间，看着扎克伯格作为政府起诉Meta案中的第一位明星证人出庭作证。

sentences.en: And when I go back, he will finish up and then we will have the former chief operating officer, Sheryl Sandberg, testify.
sentences.zh: 等我回去后，他将结束作证，接下来我们将迎来前首席运营官雪莉·桑德伯格的证词。

sentences.en: What's the first week been like?
sentences.zh: 第一周的情况怎么样？

sentences.en: It's been pretty crazy.
sentences.zh: 相当疯狂。

sentences.en: Long lines to get into the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 进入法庭的队伍排得很长。

sentences.en: The courtroom itself is full of Meta's many, many lawyers, as well as the FTC's lawyers and media and a lot of just people from the public.
sentences.zh: 法庭里挤满了Meta的众多律师，还有联邦贸易委员会的律师、媒体以及许多公众。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because up until really the minutes before the trial began, I wasn't even sure that it was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，直到审判开始前的几分钟，我甚至都不确定它是否真的会发生。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么说？

sentences.en: In recent weeks, senior Facebook officials have been trying to get the White House to stop this case from going to trial.
sentences.zh: 最近几周，Facebook的高层一直在试图游说白宫阻止这起案件进入审判阶段。

sentences.en: And recently, as reported, Mark Zuckerberg was at the White House himself meeting with the president and his top aides, trying to get the president to drop this case before it
sentences.zh: 据报道，马克·扎克伯格本人最近曾前往白宫会见总统及其高级助手，试图让总统在案件

sentences.en: could go to trial.
sentences.zh: 进入审判前撤诉。

sentences.en: And so this case, which has huge implications, can be seen as a reflection of this ongoing and strange relationship between these two men, Zuckerberg and President Trump.
sentences.zh: 因此，这起影响深远的案件，可以被视为扎克伯格与特朗普总统这两位男士之间持续且奇怪关系的缩影。

sentences.en: It's sort of surprising to hear what you're saying because we've talked on the show about how the big tech giants have been increasingly cozying up to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 听到你这么说有点令人惊讶，因为我们在节目中讨论过大型科技巨头是如何越来越向特朗普总统靠拢的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people, myself included, saw photos of Zuckerberg at the inauguration.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人，包括我在内，都看到了扎克伯格出席就职典礼的照片。

sentences.en: I sort of had the impression that these two men were at least a little bit warm toward each other.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得这两个人至少对彼此还算友好。

sentences.en: So maybe you could just unpack this a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许你能稍微拆解一下这件事。

sentences.en: What exactly is their relationship and how has it affected this case?
sentences.zh: 他们的关系究竟如何？又是如何影响这起案件的？

sentences.en: So it's interesting, the story of Zuckerberg and Trump really goes back almost a decade and their relationship has really changed and evolved over those years.
sentences.zh: 很有意思，扎克伯格和特朗普的故事其实可以追溯到近十年前，他们的关系在这些年里确实发生了变化和演变。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that what started as a story of two very powerful, but very different and maybe even opposing figures has turned into something quite different.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，最初两个非常强大但截然不同、甚至可能对立的人物之间的故事，已经演变成了完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: Lately, Zuckerberg has been very positive about Trump.
sentences.zh: 最近，扎克伯格对特朗普的态度非常积极。

sentences.en: He's really tried to get into Trump's inner circle, but Trump at this point has not returned the same sort of interest nor affection.
sentences.zh: 他确实试图进入特朗普的核心圈子，但特朗普目前并没有表现出同样的兴趣或好感。

sentences.en: I would say that the relationship is pretty one-sided at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想说，目前这种关系是相当单方面的。

sentences.en: Zuckerberg, for most of Facebook's history, has never been overtly political.
sentences.zh: 在Facebook的大部分历史中，扎克伯格从未表现出明显的政治倾向。

sentences.en: It's actually sort of a mystery as to how he votes.
sentences.zh: 他如何投票实际上是个谜。

sentences.en: He donates to both parties.
sentences.zh: 他向两党都捐过款。

sentences.en: He's not particularly vocal about politics generally.
sentences.zh: 他通常对政治并不特别发表意见。

sentences.en: Things get a little bit more complicated when it comes to Trump's first election victory in 2016.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到特朗普在2016年的首次胜选时，情况就变得复杂了一些。

sentences.en: That was a huge deal for Facebook, but not necessarily in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 这对Facebook来说是一件大事，但不一定是积极的。

sentences.en: I remember that.
sentences.zh: 我记得那件事。

sentences.en: Facebook was really widely seen as one of the reasons that Trump won the election.
sentences.zh: Facebook被广泛认为是特朗普赢得大选的原因之一。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The left blamed Facebook for Trump's victory.
sentences.zh: 左派指责Facebook导致了特朗普的胜利。

sentences.en: They say that there was a surge of political misinformation that really helped Trump in winning.
sentences.zh: 他们说政治虚假信息的激增确实帮助特朗普赢得了选举。

sentences.en: And Zuckerberg reacts to these concerns by creating new policies and new changes to the
sentences.zh: 扎克伯格通过制定新政策和对平台进行新变革来回应这些担忧，

sentences.en: platform, instituting things like fact-checking, all with the purpose of trying to slow the spread of misinformation on the site.
sentences.zh: 引入了事实核查等措施，所有这些都是为了试图减缓虚假信息在网站上的传播。

sentences.en: And the right hates this.
sentences.zh: 而右派对此深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: They say that these actions are essentially censorship and censorship of conservatives.
sentences.zh: 他们说这些行为本质上是审查，是对保守派的审查。

sentences.en: They say that the company's leaders and their employees are liberal and they have a bias that's against conservatives in Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们说公司的领导层和员工都是自由派，对保守派和特朗普有偏见。

sentences.en: And Trump comes out for the first time as anti-Facebook.
sentences.zh: 特朗普第一次公开表达了反Facebook的立场。

sentences.en: It sounds like hating Facebook basically becomes like a bipartisan issue at this point.
sentences.zh: 听起来讨厌Facebook基本上成了两党共识。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At this point, we're starting to see Facebook getting caught in between both political parties.
sentences.zh: 此时，我们开始看到Facebook夹在了两个政党之间。

sentences.en: And eventually, the Federal Trade Commission under the Trump administration decides to sue in
sentences.zh: 最终，特朗普政府领导下的联邦贸易委员会决定在2020年12月提起诉讼，

sentences.en: December 2020, which was right before they leave office.
sentences.zh: 那就在他们离任前夕。

sentences.en: That lawsuit leads to the trial that I've been covering this week.
sentences.zh: 那场诉讼导致了本周我一直在报道的审判。

sentences.en: And then on January 6th, we know what happens.
sentences.zh: 然后是1月6日，我们都知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Trump's supporters stormed the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的支持者冲击了国会大厦。

sentences.en: And at first, he is urging the crowds.
sentences.zh: 起初，他还在鼓动人群。

sentences.en: And while his supporters are in the Capitol building and police are trying to take control of the situation, Trump addresses his supporters in a video.
sentences.zh: 当他的支持者在国会大厦内，而警察试图控制局势时，特朗普在一段视频中向他的支持者发表了讲话。

sentences.en: I know you're paying.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们很痛苦。

sentences.en: I know you're hurt.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们受了伤。

sentences.en: We had an election that was stolen from us.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了一场被窃取的选举。

sentences.en: It was a landslide election.
sentences.zh: 那是一场压倒性的胜利。

sentences.en: And everyone knows it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: That video is posted across social media, including Facebook and Instagram.
sentences.zh: 那段视频被发布在包括Facebook和Instagram在内的社交媒体上。

sentences.en: People in law and order.
sentences.zh: 法律和秩序的人们。

sentences.en: We don't want anybody hurt.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望任何人受伤。

sentences.en: It's a very tough period of time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: There's never been a time like this where.
sentences.zh: 从来没有过这样的时刻。

sentences.en: And employees of the company, as well as the public, are very concerned with Trump's speech.
sentences.zh: 公司的员工以及公众都对特朗普的言论感到非常担忧。

sentences.en: What Facebook decides to do next is very important.
sentences.zh: Facebook接下来决定做什么非常重要。

sentences.en: They decide to remove those videos and they cite a policy that the company has on speech.
sentences.zh: 他们决定删除这些视频，并引用了公司关于言论的政策。

sentences.en: The company forbids any sort of incitement of violence.
sentences.zh: 公司禁止任何形式的煽动暴力。

sentences.en: And then Facebook escalates.
sentences.zh: 然后Facebook升级了行动。

sentences.en: Facebook decides to remove Trump entirely off the platform.
sentences.zh: Facebook决定将特朗普彻底从平台上移除。

sentences.en: Trump interprets that as a shot across the bow.
sentences.zh: 特朗普将其解读为一种警告。

sentences.en: And at that point, he determines that Facebook is an enemy.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他认定Facebook是敌人。

sentences.en: But when President Biden comes into office, all of a sudden, it is Zuckerberg feeling like
sentences.zh: 但当拜登总统上任后，突然间，感觉到Facebook正在被审查的人变成了扎克伯格。

sentences.en: Facebook is being censored.
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 真正的爆发点是在新冠疫情期间。

sentences.en: The real flashpoint was during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当时拜登白宫联系了Facebook的高管，并严厉要求他们打击与病毒相关的虚假信息。

sentences.en: And when the Biden White House was reaching out to Facebook senior executives and really railing on them to clamp down on misinformation related to the virus.
sentences.zh: 据扎克伯格和Meta的员工称，拜登政府对他们认为的虚假信息非常严格，

sentences.en: The Biden administration, according to Zuckerberg and employees at Meta, was quite strict about what kind of
sentences.zh: 包括任何对疫苗的怀疑，以及任何围绕新冠的对话，

sentences.en: information that they thought was misinformation, any sort of skepticism about the vaccine, as well as any sort of
sentences.zh: 即使只是提出疑问，甚至是讽刺或其他观点，他们都认为是不被允许的。

sentences.en: conversation even around COVID where there might have been either just questions raised or maybe even satirical or other justices that they did not have been in the book.
sentences.zh: 事实上，拜登政府和白宫官员告诉Meta他们需要删除所有这些内容，

sentences.en: And in fact, the relationship between the Biden administration and White House officials were telling Meta that they need to take down all that content,
sentences.zh: Meta认为这是一种严重的越权。

sentences.en: which Meta thought was a real overreach.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Meta与拜登政府的关系在拜登任命了一位真正的反垄断斗士莉娜·汗担任其最高反垄断监管机构负责人后变得更糟了。

sentences.en: And in fact, the relationship between Meta and the Biden administration only gets worse once Biden appoints a real trust buster, Lena Kahn, to be his top antitrust regulator.
sentences.zh: 莉娜在反垄断法这个狭小而深奥的世界里是一位知名人物。

sentences.en: Lena is a well-known figure within the very small and esoteric world of antitrust law.
sentences.zh: 她被视为整个美国企业界最大的威胁之一。

sentences.en: And she is seen as one of the biggest threats across corporate America.
sentences.zh: 莉娜·汗接手了特朗普政府时期发起的针对Meta的反垄断诉讼。

sentences.en: And Lena Kahn picks up that antitrust suit against Meta that was initiated in the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，此时此刻，扎克伯格和拜登政府之间的分歧已经大到不能再大了。

sentences.en: So it sounds like at this point, basically, Zuckerberg and the Biden administration could not be farther apart.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府与Meta之间的敌意与日俱增。

sentences.en: The animosity between the Biden administration and Meta only grows.
sentences.zh: 公司感觉自己成了众矢之的。

sentences.en: And the company's feeling very much like a target.
sentences.zh: 那么，随着扎克伯格与拜登的关系恶化，他与特朗普的关系在此时又如何呢？

sentences.en: So as Zuckerberg's relationship with Biden is deteriorating, what's going on with his relationship to Trump at this point in time?
sentences.zh: 嗯，真正的转折点是针对特朗普的暗杀未遂事件。

sentences.en: Well, the real inflection point was the assassination attempt on Trump.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，马克·扎克伯格看到特朗普从宾夕法尼亚州的舞台上站起来，挥舞着拳头，脸上流着血。

sentences.en: And that was a moment when Mark Zuckerberg saw Trump emerge and stand up from that stage in Pennsylvania with his fist pumped in the air, blood coming down his face.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，看到唐纳德·特朗普在脸部中弹后站起来。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, seeing Donald Trump get up after getting shot in the face.
sentences.zh: 扎克伯格后来评论说，他认为那是一个英雄主义的时刻。

sentences.en: Zuckerberg later commented that he thought that was such a moment of heroism.
sentences.zh: 这是我一生中见过的最硬核的事情之一。

sentences.en: One of the most badass things I've ever seen in my life.
sentences.zh: 他用他的话来说，特朗普是个真正的硬汉。

sentences.en: And that he thought that, in his words, that Trump was a real badass.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，作为一个美国人，很难不对那种精神和斗志感到动容。

sentences.en: At some level, as an American, it's like hard to not get kind of emotional about that spirit and that fight.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么很多人喜欢这个家伙的原因。

sentences.en: And I think that that's why a lot of people like the guy.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次听到扎克伯格如此积极地谈论一位政治候选人。

sentences.en: And that was the first time that I'd heard Zuckerberg really speak out so positively about a political candidate.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直非常小心，不在政治上采取任何强硬立场。

sentences.en: He'd been very careful for many years to not take any strong position in politics.
sentences.zh: 而在2024年大选之后，事情真的开始升温了。

sentences.en: And then after the 2024 election, things really start to pick up.
sentences.zh: 我们看到扎克伯格几乎在竞相展示他对特朗普的喜爱。

sentences.en: We see Zuckerberg almost racing to show his affection for Trump.
sentences.zh: Facebook创始人马克·扎克伯格今天在海湖庄园与当选总统进行了私人会晤。

sentences.en: Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg had a private meeting with the president-elect today at Mar-a-Lago.
sentences.zh: 首先，他公开祝贺总统当选。

sentences.en: First, he publicly congratulates the president on his election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，马克·扎克伯格来看过我，并且……

sentences.en: Well, Mark Zuckerberg's been over to see me and...
sentences.zh: 他拜访了海湖庄园的当选总统。

sentences.en: He visits the president-elect in Mar-a-Lago.
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 你知道，轻松的一周。

sentences.en: You know, chill week.
sentences.zh: 是的，算是吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, sort of.
sentences.zh: 他上了乔·罗根的播客。

sentences.en: He goes on the Joe Rogan podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我对特朗普总统感到乐观的一点是，我认为他只是想让美国赢。

sentences.en: And it's one of the things that I'm optimistic about with President Trump is I think he just wants America to win.
sentences.zh: 并且在相当长的一段时间里，他谈到了他是多么钦佩总统。

sentences.en: And for quite some time, talks about how much he admired the president.
sentences.zh: 这些来自拜登政府的人会打电话给我们的团队，大喊大叫并咒骂。

sentences.en: These people from the Biden administration would call up our team and, like, scream at them and curse.
sentences.zh: 就像这些……

sentences.en: And it's like these...
sentences.zh: 以及他是如何对民主党领导的前白宫感到如此沮丧的。

sentences.en: And how he had become so frustrated with the Democratic-led former White House.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好。

sentences.en: Hey, everyone.
sentences.zh: 今天我想谈谈一件重要的事情。

sentences.en: I want to talk about something important today.
sentences.zh: 我们看到扎克伯格也在公司内部改变政策。

sentences.en: We see Zuckerberg also change policies within the company.
sentences.zh: 这是我们要做的。

sentences.en: Here's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们将取消事实核查员，并从美国开始，用类似于X的社区注释来取代他们。

sentences.en: First, we're going to get rid of fact-checkers and replace them with community notes similar to X starting in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他取消了事实核查。

sentences.en: He gets rid of fact-checking.
sentences.zh: 最初旨在更具包容性的运动，却越来越多地被用来压制意见和排斥持有不同想法的人。

sentences.en: What started as a movement to be more inclusive has increasingly been used to shut down opinions and shut out people with different ideas.
sentences.zh: 这已经走得太远了。

sentences.en: And it's gone too far.
sentences.zh: 他还取消了公司内部的DEI（多元、公平、包容）相关工作。

sentences.en: And he also gets rid of DEI, diversity, equity, inclusion, sort of efforts at the company.
sentences.zh: 最近的选举也让人感觉是一个文化转折点，再次优先考虑言论自由。

sentences.en: The recent elections also feel like a cultural tipping point towards once again prioritizing speech.
sentences.zh: 这两项重大政策变化似乎与特朗普的议程非常一致。

sentences.en: These two big policy changes seem very much aligned with the Trump agenda.
sentences.zh: 关于特朗普如何从被排斥者变成权势人物的绝佳例子，看看Meta就知道了。

sentences.en: And for a prime example of how Trump went from pariah to powerful, look to Meta.
sentences.zh: 公司证实，它向特朗普的就职基金捐赠了一百万美元。

sentences.en: The company confirms it made a million-dollar contribution to Trump's inaugural fund.
sentences.zh: （注：此条目对应原输入中的第149条，已完成翻译）

sentences.en: Meta donates a million dollars to the Trump inauguration.
sentences.zh: Meta向特朗普的就职典礼捐赠了一百万美元。

sentences.en: He's really pulling out all the stops.
sentences.zh: 他真的是在竭尽全力。

sentences.en: He's pulling out all the stops.
sentences.zh: 他正在竭尽全力。

sentences.en: It's happening in rapid fire all within a compressed few weeks.
sentences.zh: 这一切都在短短几周内密集地发生。

sentences.en: And, you know, whether or not he believes in President Trump or whether he's just trying to do the best thing for his companies,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，无论他是否真的相信特朗普总统，还是他只是想为自己的公司做最好的打算，

sentences.en: I guess that doesn't really matter because he's gone full MAGA, right?
sentences.zh: 我想这其实并不重要，因为他已经彻底“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like he's fully aligning himself with the new administration.
sentences.zh: 就像他正在与新政府全面靠拢一样。

sentences.en: But I have to note that looking at where we are today, it doesn't seem like any of that helped him that much.
sentences.zh: 但我必须指出，看看我们今天的处境，这一切似乎并没有给他带来多大帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, Rachel, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，雷切尔，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: The president still holds a grudge against Zuckerberg and Meta.
sentences.zh: 总统仍然对扎克伯格和Meta怀恨在心。

sentences.en: And as somebody very close to the president told me just a few days ago, the president still wants his pound of flesh.
sentences.zh: 正如一位与总统关系非常密切的人几天前告诉我的那样，总统仍然想要报复。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Cecilia, we just talked about how Zuckerberg couldn't get Trump to make this case go away.
sentences.zh: 那么，塞西莉亚，我们刚才谈到了扎克伯格无法让特朗普撤销这起诉讼。

sentences.en: But what exactly is the case that the government is bringing here?
sentences.zh: 但政府在这里提出的诉讼到底是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, this case is really pretty novel in that this all centers around two acquisitions more than a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 是的，这起案件确实非常新颖，因为它完全围绕着十多年前的两起收购案展开。

sentences.en: The acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp.
sentences.zh: 即对Instagram和WhatsApp的收购。

sentences.en: And what the federal government is arguing is that Facebook had a monopoly when they bought these companies.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府的论点是，Facebook在收购这些公司时已经处于垄断地位。

sentences.en: And through these acquisitions, they were able to keep their monopoly.
sentences.zh: 通过这些收购，他们得以维持了自己的垄断地位。

sentences.en: The reason why that is such a eyebrow-raising argument in particular is because the very agency that is suing Meta was the agency that approved those mergers more than a decade ago in the first place.
sentences.zh: 之所以这个论点特别令人惊讶，是因为起诉Meta的正是十多年前批准这些合并案的同一个机构。

sentences.en: Okay, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好的，解释一下。

sentences.en: So, I've got to take you back in a time machine to around 2011, 2012.
sentences.zh: 所以，我得带你坐时光机回到2011年、2012年左右。

sentences.en: And this was a really pivotal time for Facebook.
sentences.zh: 这对Facebook来说是一个非常关键的时期。

sentences.en: Facebook really struggled to create an app for the smartphone.
sentences.zh: Facebook当时在开发智能手机应用方面确实很吃力。

sentences.en: And they were starting to see competition, particularly from Instagram, that made Mark Zuckerberg very nervous.
sentences.zh: 他们开始感受到竞争，尤其是来自Instagram的竞争，这让马克·扎克伯格非常紧张。

sentences.en: Because Instagram had this new and very interesting photo-sharing app.
sentences.zh: 因为Instagram当时拥有这款新颖且非常有趣的图片分享应用。

sentences.en: And so, Zuckerberg, in 2012, decided to buy Instagram, which didn't have that many users and had very few employees, for a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 因此，扎克伯格在2012年决定以10亿美元的价格收购Instagram，当时它并没有多少用户，员工也很少。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That in itself was a big deal at that time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时本身就是一件大事。

sentences.en: But regulators thought that it was such a small company, Instagram, and it didn't directly compete with Facebook as a social network,
sentences.zh: 但监管机构认为Instagram只是一家小公司，而且它并没有直接作为社交网络与Facebook竞争，

sentences.en: that they felt comfortable allowing that merger to go through.
sentences.zh: 所以他们觉得可以放心地批准那次合并。

sentences.en: And then Zuckerberg got nervous again.
sentences.zh: 然后扎克伯格又紧张起来了。

sentences.en: Around 2014, he saw the rise of messaging apps like WeChat in China and WhatsApp, which was an app that was very popular globally,
sentences.zh: 2014年左右，他看到了像中国的微信和WhatsApp这类即时通讯应用的兴起，WhatsApp在全球非常受欢迎，

sentences.en: really picking up steam and getting tons of users around the world.
sentences.zh: 势头强劲，在全球拥有大量用户。

sentences.en: And he was afraid that those kinds of messaging apps could also compete with Facebook because they could take on more social features like sharing between friends and family.
sentences.zh: 他担心这类通讯应用也会与Facebook竞争，因为它们可以承载更多社交功能，比如在亲友间分享内容。

sentences.en: So then, in 2014, he buys WhatsApp for $19 billion.
sentences.zh: 于是，在2014年，他以190亿美元收购了WhatsApp。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Huge price tag that drew a ton of interest at the time.
sentences.zh: 这个高昂的价格在当时引起了极大的关注。

sentences.en: But again, regulators said, you know, this app doesn't directly compete with Facebook, so, yes, we'll approve it.
sentences.zh: 但监管机构再次表示，你知道，这个应用并没有直接与Facebook竞争，所以，是的，我们批准它。

sentences.en: So, both mergers approved by the Federal Trade Commission.
sentences.zh: 所以，这两起合并案都得到了联邦贸易委员会的批准。

sentences.en: So, it sounds like from what you're saying that there weren't any alarm bells ringing at the time when Facebook was acquiring these companies.
sentences.zh: 听你这么说，好像在Facebook收购这些公司时，并没有敲响任何警钟。

sentences.en: But obviously, something changed.
sentences.zh: 但显然，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: What changed, what changed, and why?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么变化，为什么会变？

sentences.en: Well, a couple things changed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几件事变了。

sentences.en: First, Facebook becomes very powerful.
sentences.zh: 首先，Facebook变得非常强大。

sentences.en: It hits 3.5 billion users.
sentences.zh: 它拥有了35亿用户。

sentences.en: And that sheer scale puts a spotlight on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 这种巨大的规模让Facebook成为了焦点。

sentences.en: Suddenly, people see that it has become an essential place for so many people around the world to obtain and to share information.
sentences.zh: 突然间，人们意识到它已经成为全球许多人获取和分享信息的重要场所。

sentences.en: And once people start recognizing that, especially around the 2016 and 2020 elections, it changes the perception of Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg.
sentences.zh: 一旦人们开始意识到这一点，特别是在2016年和2020年大选前后，人们对Facebook和马克·扎克伯格的看法就改变了。

sentences.en: The other thing that changes is that regulators start looking at the Silicon Valley companies very differently.
sentences.zh: 另一个变化是，监管机构开始以完全不同的眼光看待硅谷公司。

sentences.en: They see that they see that these Internet giants only get bigger and stronger in ways that are unexpected.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这些互联网巨头只会以意想不到的方式变得越来越大、越来越强。

sentences.en: They start to look at acquisitions that these companies have made over the years that may have not seemed either threatening or anti-competitive at the time because these big companies are often buying very small startups.
sentences.zh: 他们开始审视这些公司多年来进行的收购，这些收购在当时看起来似乎既没有威胁性也不反竞争，因为这些大公司往往是在收购非常小的初创企业。

sentences.en: But those acquisitions become really important tools for these companies to continue to grow and to maintain their monopolies.
sentences.zh: 但这些收购成为了这些公司继续增长和维持垄断地位的重要工具。

sentences.en: It used to be that the key way to determine if a monopoly was breaking the law was whether prices were going up for consumers.
sentences.zh: 过去，判断垄断是否违法的关键标准是消费者的价格是否上涨。

sentences.en: But how does that apply to an Internet company, especially a company that has apps like Facebook and Instagram, which are free?
sentences.zh: 但这如何适用于互联网公司，特别是像Facebook和Instagram这样提供免费应用的公司呢？

sentences.en: And so regulators are saying there are different ways that we should look at how these companies have too much power.
sentences.zh: 因此，监管机构表示，我们应该从不同的角度来看待这些公司如何拥有了过大的权力。

sentences.en: So what is the harm that the government is arguing that Meta poses here exactly, if not ripping people off in terms of how much they're paying for a product?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果不是在消费者支付的产品价格上坑人，政府认为Meta在这里构成的危害到底是什么？

sentences.en: So the government is arguing that there are other ways consumers have been harmed.
sentences.zh: 政府认为消费者还受到了其他方面的伤害。

sentences.en: They say that if these mergers were not approved,
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果这些合并案没有被批准，

sentences.en: that maybe Instagram and WhatsApp would have created much more competition that would spur Facebook to be more innovative and to make their app better.
sentences.zh: 也许Instagram和WhatsApp会创造出更多的竞争，从而激励Facebook进行更多创新，并改进其应用。

sentences.en: So you might see fewer things like data privacy scandals.
sentences.zh: 这样你可能会看到更少的数据隐私丑闻。

sentences.en: You might see the company do a better job when it comes to containing misinformation.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到该公司在遏制虚假信息方面做得更好。

sentences.en: All these things that are not related to price, but do affect the consumer experience.
sentences.zh: 所有这些与价格无关，但确实影响了消费者体验的事情。

sentences.en: And most interestingly, the Trump administration has introduced a new wrinkle.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的是，特朗普政府引入了一个新的转折点。

sentences.en: President Trump and his top antitrust regulators have argued that these platforms censor speech and that their ability to censor speech is a real sign, a symptom of a problem,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统及其高级反垄断监管机构认为，这些平台审查言论，而它们审查言论的能力是一个真正的迹象，是问题的一个症状，

sentences.en: which is that they are too powerful.
sentences.zh: 那就是它们太强大了。

sentences.en: So they are arguing for the first time that I have heard a speech theory that antitrust enforcement should include concerns about speech.
sentences.zh: 所以他们第一次提出了我所听到的关于言论的理论，即反垄断执法应该包括对言论问题的关注。

sentences.en: Cecilia, I can't help but notice that Zuckerberg, who has become this, like,
sentences.zh: 塞西莉亚，我忍不住注意到扎克伯格，他已经成为了一个，就像，

sentences.en: free speech absolutist and rolled back so much of the company's past efforts to censor content on the platform, he's actually now the target of a case.
sentences.zh: 言论自由的绝对主义者，并撤回了公司过去在平台上审查内容的许多努力，他现在实际上成了诉讼的目标。

sentences.en: The president or his administration is taking on, at least in part, because he thinks Meta holds too much power to shape speech.
sentences.zh: 总统或其政府之所以采取行动，至少部分是因为他认为Meta拥有过大的权力来塑造言论。

sentences.en: So it's really ironic.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很讽刺。

sentences.en: In some ways, Zuckerberg and Trump want the same thing.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，扎克伯格和特朗普想要的是一样的东西。

sentences.en: They want complete free speech on the internet.
sentences.zh: 他们想要互联网上的完全言论自由。

sentences.en: They want no censorship.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要任何审查。

sentences.en: And Zuckerberg has tried to signal to Trump that, hey, we are on the same side on this issue.
sentences.zh: 扎克伯格试图向特朗普发出信号，嘿，在这个问题上我们是站在同一边的。

sentences.en: But even though Zuckerberg has tried to do that and made so many other efforts to try to appease Trump, it really hasn't landed in the way that Zuckerberg wants and needs.
sentences.zh: 但尽管扎克伯格试图这样做，并做出了许多其他努力来安抚特朗普，但这并没有产生扎克伯格想要和需要的效果。

sentences.en: He still has to go through this trial.
sentences.zh: 他仍然必须经历这场审判。

sentences.en: And that's because even though they might agree on some things, Facebook is still viewed as simply just too big.
sentences.zh: 这是因为即使他们在某些事情上可能达成一致，Facebook仍然被认为太大了。

sentences.en: But it sort of sounds like from what you've explained that the government has a bit of an uphill battle here for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 但听了你的解释，感觉政府在这里面临着一场硬仗，原因有二。

sentences.en: One, they basically have to say, like, look, even though we approved these mergers back in the day, we've changed our mind.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们基本上必须说，看，尽管我们当年批准了这些合并，但我们改变主意了。

sentences.en: We want to unwind them, which seems tough.
sentences.zh: 我们想要拆分它们，这看起来很难。

sentences.en: And two, they've also got this new argument where they're trying to prove new harms in a theory that's kind of been untested before, right?
sentences.zh: 第二，他们还有一个新的论点，试图在一个以前未经检验的理论中证明新的危害，对吧？

sentences.en: So should I take it from what you've just said that Meta is feeling pretty good about its chances here?
sentences.zh: 那么，我是否可以从你刚才说的话中理解为，Meta对在这里胜诉感觉相当不错？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think Meta is coming in really confidently.
sentences.zh: 我认为Meta表现得非常有信心。

sentences.en: I think legal experts are all saying that this is a tough case for the FTC.
sentences.zh: 我认为法律专家都说这对联邦贸易委员会来说是一个棘手的案件。

sentences.en: But the real question that I have as I watched Mark Zuckerberg finish his testimony this week is, what is he winning here?
sentences.zh: 但我看着马克·扎克伯格本周结束作证时，我真正的问题是，他在这里赢得了什么？

sentences.en: They might win this trial, but he still needs to win over the president.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会赢得这场审判，但他仍然需要赢得总统的支持。

sentences.en: There are so many other issues that relate to his business.
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他与他的业务相关的问题。

sentences.en: And there's so much at stake with this administration as the company continues to try to expand new areas and grow.
sentences.zh: 随着公司继续尝试扩展新领域并实现增长，本届政府的决策对公司来说至关重要。

sentences.en: So I would say this is just one step in a very long process for Meta to really get back into the good graces of Washington and particularly to, for the first time,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这只是Meta真正重获华盛顿青睐，特别是第一次赢得特朗普支持的漫长过程中的一小步，

sentences.en: win over Trump's support.
sentences.zh: 赢得特朗普的支持。

sentences.en: Because who knows what the next fight will be.
sentences.zh: 因为谁知道下一场战斗会是什么。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there will be many.
sentences.zh: 而且还会有很多场。

sentences.en: Cecilia, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 塞西莉亚，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，雷切尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: A federal judge threatened to open a contempt investigation into whether the Trump administration violated an order the judge issued directing officials to stop planes of Venezuelan migrants from being sent to El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 一名联邦法官威胁要对特朗普政府是否违反了法官发布的命令展开藐视法庭调查，该命令指示官员停止将委内瑞拉移民的飞机送往萨尔瓦多。

sentences.en: The judge said he would begin the proceedings against the administration unless the White House gives scores of Venezuelan men deported to El Salvador a chance to challenge their removal.
sentences.zh: 法官表示，除非白宫给被驱逐到萨尔瓦多的数十名委内瑞拉男子一个挑战其驱逐令的机会，否则他将对政府启动诉讼程序。

sentences.en: And on Wednesday, Britain's Supreme Court ruled that trans women do not fall within the legal definition of women under the country's equality legislation,
sentences.zh: 周三，英国最高法院裁定，跨性别女性不属于该国平等立法中“女性”的法律定义，

sentences.en: dealing a major blow to campaigners for transgender rights.
sentences.zh: 这对跨性别权利运动者造成了重大打击。

sentences.en: While the five judges involved in the ruling said the legal definition of a woman is based on biological sex,
sentences.zh: 虽然参与裁决的五位法官表示，女性的法律定义基于生理性别，

sentences.en: they emphasized that they were not commenting on whether trans women are women more broadly, saying it was not the role of the court to adjudicate the meaning of gender or sex.
sentences.zh: 但他们强调，他们并未评论跨性别女性在更广泛意义上是否为女性，称法院的角色并非裁定性别或性别的含义。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Nina Feldman and Carlos Prieto.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由尼娜·费尔德曼和卡洛斯·普列托制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Brendan Klinkenberg and Mark George, with help from Mike Benoit.
sentences.zh: 由布伦丹·克林肯伯格和马克·乔治编辑，迈克·贝努瓦提供协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Pat McCusker, Diane Wong, Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 包含帕特·麦卡斯克、黛安·王、马里昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonder League.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonder League的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场痛苦、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。
